title: Preserve a valid guest observation when bridge requests remain pending
description: Host-session prerequisite of97341ad5. Own scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs and scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Today child close exit0 becomes SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION solely because session.pending.length>0, even after valid hello/observation/clean EOF; stop already aborts forwards and closes stdin. Make authenticated supervisor terminal observation+clean EOF+exit0 finalize once while cancelling/abandoning unresolved agent requests; never replay a request, dispatch queued work after terminal completion, or write late replies to closed stdin. Preserve real provider/protocol/timeout/abort failures and every malformed/duplicate/trailing-frame guard; cancellation cannot erase a prior failure or claim an upstream side effect was undone. Test pending active and queued forwards at successful finish, late resolve/reject/abort races, no extra forward/reply/onObservation, and negative no-observation/nonzero/partial/trailing-frame cases. Use existing stop/controller/timer ownership, no second session queue. Do not modify GUARD/pump or certification. Full external snapshot gate: node --test scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs && (cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test). Depend on containment and provider-resolution task for explicit source serialization; parent follows this test file.
definitionOfDone: Valid hello/one observation/clean EOF/exit0 succeeds once despite unresolved agent requests; pending work is cancelled without late forwarding/writes.
Malformed framing, missing observation, nonzero exit, real timeout/abort and pre-existing failures remain failures in race-focused tests.
No leaked timers/listeners or repeated side effects; full runner+daemon regression passes in an external snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST, in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs (DoD 1-3). Load test-driven-development. Use only the existing fakeProvider, openSession, exchange and until helpers and the HELLO/REQUEST/EXIT frames. Add no new harness.

1. Flip the one held H4 row that encodes the old contract. Locate it by its comment, 'An answer still owed when the job ends leaves the session unclean, so no observation is delivered': its forward never settles, then EXIT and exit(0). It now resolves {observation: EXIT, executionReady: false} and delivers onObservation exactly once. Nothing is written after the job frame (proc.written stays []), forwarded has length 1, and that forward's signal is aborted. Update the comment. No other H1-H8 row changes.

2. New test 'H9 a clean finish abandons pending requests: in-flight forwards are aborted, queued ones are never forwarded, and nothing is written late'. Each case asserts the result, run.observations, run.forwarded, proc.written and proc.kills, and that the caller signal's abort listeners are 0 after settle (getEventListeners).
- Active and queued: REQUEST id 1, whose forward never settles, plus id 2 queued behind it, then EXIT and exit(0). The run succeeds once; only id 1 was forwarded; nothing was written; its signal is aborted.
- Late settle after the finish: the forward resolves, or rejects, after `await run.promise`. After a further tick, still no write and no second onObservation.
- Abort-aware forward: it rejects as soon as its signal aborts. The session succeeds and no refusal frame is written.
- A forward still hanging past timeoutMs after the finish, while the provider exits 0 at once: success. Wait timeoutMs plus 50 ms and assert no kill and no late write, so no live timer acted.
- A forward that settles just before the EOF is answered once (written 1), then success: a reply is written at most once and never after the finish.
- A reply write in flight when the EOF lands (fake `write` callback delayed until after exit) does not fail the session.
3. Negatives in the same test, each with a request pending, each a failure with no observation delivered:
- EOF without an observation, or a trailing partial frame at EOF: SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION;
- exit(1): SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED;
- a frame after the observation: SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION;
- a forward timing out BEFORE the EOF (timeoutMs 100), then EXIT and exit(0): SESSION_TIMEOUT, because the prior failure is kept;
- a caller abort after the observation and EOF but before the provider exits: SESSION_ABORTED;
- a job-frame write that fails (fake `first`): still SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED.

Run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` and record the RED rows in the step note. At RED, the flipped H4 row and every H9 success case fail with SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. The negatives pass at RED and must stay green.
implementationPlan.note:
Tests first, in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs only.
- H4 'unanswered' row flipped: it now resolves {observation: EXIT, executionReady:false} with observations [EXIT], written [], forwarded 1 and its signal aborted. No other H1-H8 row changed.
- openSession's forward wrapper now also passes {signal} to answer as a 3rd arg, for the abort-aware row. Existing answers ignore it.
- New H9 helpers, all local to H9: owe, finish, succeeds, fails. owe also spies on stdin.write and counts calls made after stdin was destroyed (proc.late).
- H9 success cases: active+queued; late resolve; late reject; abort-aware forward; hang past timeoutMs (500, then wait 550); settle-before-EOF (written 1); in-flight reply write failed by teardown; in-flight reply write that succeeds after settle.
- H9 negatives, each with a request owed: no observation; trailing partial frame; exit 1; frame after the observation; timeout before EOF then exit 0; caller abort after the clean EOF; job-frame write failing after the clean EOF.
RED, focused run (node 24.21.0, env -i, --test-name-pattern '^H[0-9] '): 9 tests, 7 pass, 2 fail. H4 and H9 fail with SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
Per-case RED, in scratch /tmp/moe-5ee8-red.z6Lm with succeeds and asserts made non-fatal: all 8 success cases fail. Seven give SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION; the teardown-failed in-flight write gives SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED through pump's catch. All 7 negatives pass at RED.
Peer dirty paths I left alone: .moe/tasks/{16bbf8ff,a4a729dd,b319b263,f4811a72}.json, scripts/moe-agent.sh, .moe/decisions/.

Fix, in scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs, relay/pump only:
- The child 'close' handler no longer has `|| session.pending.length > 0`. A code 0 close succeeds when `ended && observation`; requests still owed were abandoned.
- pump's loop head is `while (pending.length > 0 && !closing)`.
- pump's catch: `if (session.closing) return;` before the TIMEOUT/PROVIDER_FAILED stop, so a deadline or reply write that teardown cut short records no code. Before closing, codes are unchanged.
- The JSDoc 'no owed reply' sentence is rewritten: in-flight forwards see their signal abort, queued ones are never forwarded, no reply is written after the finish, and an aborted forward may already have acted upstream, with nothing reporting it undone.
- Unchanged: the job-frame catch, onAbort, stop's kill timer, `failure ??=`, receive() and decoder guards, settle, and the result shape.
Test growth (bridge file): one more H9 negative, "a provider that exits 0 before its stdout reached a clean EOF" gives SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. Without it, the close-ignores-`ended` mutant survived.
GREEN:
- Full bridge file, node 24.21.0 under env -i, in place (imports only scripts/local-runner): exit 0, 65 tests, 64 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip (LA5, needs MOE_PINNED_CODEX).
- H rows: 9/9.
- H4+H9 flake loop: 8/8 runs green.
Mutation sweep in scratch /tmp/moe-5ee8-mut.79Q1, H rows, scored by exit code:
- Killed 8/9: pending check restored (H4, H9); catch ignores closing (H9); failure `=` instead of `??=` (H2, H4, H9, H5, H6); close ignores observation (H2, H9); close ignores ended (H9, after the new row); settle keeps timers (H9); pump writes when reply returns bytes after closing (H9); stop without controller.abort (H4, H9).
- One survivor, equivalent: the loop-head `!closing`. After teardown, reply() returns null before forward and pump returns before writing, so the guard only skips a wasted health probe.
- The no-op control passes.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW of this row's diff. Load adversarial-self-review.
- Can any code path forward or write after session.closing? Check pump's loop head, reply's checks after its await, and the job-frame write.
- Can onObservation run twice, or after a failure? settle is guarded by settled.
- Is a failure recorded before teardown ever replaced or cleared? `??=` only.
- Can a timer outlive settle? settle clears session.timers, and a bounded() deadline started before teardown is cleared there too.
- Can a forward that ignores abort keep the promise unsettled? Its race stays pending, but the session settles on close.
- Does a hung provider still end as SESSION_TIMEOUT with a local SIGKILL?
- Are the receive() guards, MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS and the id replay check untouched?
- runAgentJob (agent-lifecycle.mjs) and its AJ rows still read only observation.
Error handling: fix in-scope findings here, with a test. Route out-of-scope findings to the governor with moe.add_comment on this row.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of this row's own diff (the two files only).
- Forward or write after closing: none. pump's loop head checks !closing. reply() checks closing after its daemonRefusal await, and the forward call follows synchronously. pump checks closing after reply, then starts the write synchronously. The job-frame write happens only at relay start. H9's proc.late spy (stdin.write while destroyed) stays 0 in every case.
- onObservation: settle is guarded by `settled`, and a failure rejects before onObservation. H9 asserts observations stays at length 1 after late resolve and reject.
- First failure wins: `??=` only, and the catch's closing-return never clears a code. The `=` mutant dies on H2, H4, H5, H6 and H9.
  - A TIMEOUT raised before teardown always records its code. Its rejection chain is all microtasks, which drain right after the timer callback, before any stdout 'end'.
  - A real reply-write error before teardown also reaches stdin's 'error' listener (PROVIDER_FAILED).
- Timers: closing is always true at settle, and bounded() is only ever called before a closing check, so no timer starts after settle. settle clears the rest. The keep-timers mutant dies on H9's 'past' row (no SIGKILL).
- A forward that ignores abort: the session still settles on close. Its race stays pending and is garbage once the forward settles.
- A hung provider still ends as SESSION_TIMEOUT with a local SIGKILL (H4 'killed' row).
- receive() guards, MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS and the replay check are untouched.
- runAgentJob reads only observation (agent-lifecycle.mjs:83). The AJ rows are green in the gate.
Finding fixed: the close handler's comment sat on the violation line and read as if it explained the violation. It is now one line above the handler ("Exit 0 after a clean EOF and the observation is the finish; a request still owed then was abandoned, not failed."). Comment only.
Theoretical, not new: an aborted forward whose transport ignores the signal can still land upstream after runAgentJob's sweep and lease release. That already held on every failure path; the JSDoc says nothing reports it undone.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A guest bridge session whose supervisor sent hello, exactly one observation and a clean EOF, then exited 0, resolves once with that observation even if agent requests are still pending. In-flight forwards are aborted and queued ones are never forwarded, and no reply is written after the finish. Real failures keep their codes and are never erased: malformed or extra frames, a missing observation, a nonzero or killed provider, a timeout or abort before the finish, and a job-frame write failure.
acceptanceCriteria: The flipped H4 'unanswered' row and the new H9 cases pass, as does every other H1-H8 row.
The full local-runner suites and the daemon suite pass in an external snapshot.
invariants: onObservation runs at most once, and never after a failure.
First failure wins; cancellation never clears or replaces it.
No forward and no stdin write happens after teardown begins.
compatibility: The result shape {observation, executionReady: false} and the SESSION_* codes are unchanged.
runAgentJob and the AJ rows are unaffected.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Waiting for pending forwards to settle before resolving: rejected. A forward can hang until timeoutMs, and the guest has already ended the job. The task asks to abandon them, not to drain them. 2) Reporting an abandoned-request count in the result: rejected, because it changes the {observation, executionReady} shape that runAgentJob and the H rows consume, and the DoD asks for no new field. 3) Ignoring every failure after the clean EOF: rejected. A job-frame write failure, a caller abort, a nonzero or killed provider and stop's kill-timer timeout are real and stay failures. Only pump's own teardown artifacts are dropped.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- At the clean EOF, the stdout 'end' handler calls stop(session) with no code: it sets closing, aborts the controller and destroys stdin. The child 'close' handler then decides.
- pump keeps pending[0] until its reply is written, so an aborted forward leaves pending non-empty. That is the sole cause of today's SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (the governor's 97341ad5 note cites guest-session.mjs:169).
- The held H4 'unanswered' row asserts the old contract and must be flipped. The AJ5 hello-only row in local-runner.test.mjs (no observation) stays a violation.
- Deps: a4a729dd touches guest-supervisor.py plus a new local-runner-guard.test.mjs, and 92307adc does not touch guest-session.mjs or this test file. Both edges order work, they don't share files. The parent 97341ad5 follows this row on local-runner-bridge.test.mjs.
planningNotes.risks:
- Timing-sensitive tests: drive every race with explicit promise control and until() checks, never sleep-based ordering except the single timeoutMs+50 ms no-live-timer check.
- The snapshot gate runs npm ci and a build in a temp dir (network, a few minutes). Never in the shared checkout.
